_meta.description: Static AI-written scouting reports, one per owner — the back of each trading card. Generated once from league data and not recomputed by the app.
_meta.note: Regenerated after the data audit: tie games restored, streaks computed from true game sequences.

summaries.jmuggy20: The winningest owner in league history. 140 career wins, a record thirteen playoff trips, three titles (2009, 2017, 2021) spread across three different eras, and the longest win streak ever recorded — eleven straight in 2024. Seven trips to the final is the stuff of legend; losing four of them is the stuff of therapy. And somewhere, b50rock still brings up the 147-point beating from 2014.
summaries.RichoSuave: The dynasty. Four championships — 2011, 2014, 2023, 2025 — the most banners in the rafters, with a nine-game heater carrying the 2023 run. Eleven playoff appearances and near-total ownership of Rodney19140 (9–2). Just don't ask about the 2025 crown: a 7–7 regular season remains the most mediocre path to a ring ever recorded. Royalty, but royalty that snuck in through the service entrance.
summaries.jstoll65: Two-time champion (2013, 2015) with a hidden monster season: ten straight wins in 2020 that somehow ended in yet another runner-up finish. 134 career victories, eleven playoff berths, and personal ownership of half the league (10–1 over njohnson9352, 14–5 over juicebox269). Six finals appearances is elite; losing four of them earned him the crown he never wanted: king of the bridesmaids.
summaries.kevinconklin05: The 2012 champion and author of a ten-game win streak in 2010 that stood as the league record for fourteen years. Twelve playoff appearances, 131 career victories, and a 10–3 stranglehold on Rodney19140 put him firmly among the founding-father elite. Since the title, though, it's been three runner-up finishes and a growing collection of silver medals — always the artist, rarely the closer. The 140-point flattening by juicebox269 in 2015 is not to be mentioned at the draft.
summaries.Dieselbaron: Two banners, eight years apart (2010, 2018) — proof he can win in any decade he feels like showing up for. Seventeen seasons of trench warfare with jmuggy20 in the league's longest-running rivalry (trailing 15–17), plus a six-game surge in 2020 behind his best-ever 2,051 points. The catch: an almost perfectly even 114–112 career record, a 3–11 faceplant in 2022, and a 1–6 record against frolickingjester, a man who joined the league twelve years after he did.
summaries.adrenth01: Champion in 2016 and 2020, owner of the joint-biggest blowout in history (+136 over CheezeBallHustle, whom he beat 9 times in 10 meetings — a legal form of bullying), and still ascending: a seven-game streak and a career-best 2,038 points in 2025. Seventeen seasons at 114–111–1, that lone tie dating to the league's very first year. Forever dangerous — except against jstoll65, who has beaten him 22 times and counting.
summaries.b50rock: The 2019 champion and owner of the single most violent result in league history: a +147 annihilation of jmuggy20 in 2014 that's still spoken of in hushed tones. Ten playoff berths, a 2,103-point season in 2021, and two of the league's rare tied games on his ledger (118–106–2). One banner from ten October runs is the resume of a man who peaks exactly one week too early.
summaries.juicebox269: The 2022 champion, and he did it in style — 2,135 points that season, one of the great offensive campaigns ever assembled, with a seven-game streak back in 2015 for good measure. Nine playoff trips over sixteen seasons and a habit of delivering historic beatdowns (ask kevinconklin05 about 2015). But the ledger shows a career 5–14 record against jstoll65, and a quiet exit after 2024 — the throne was rented, never owned.
summaries.MattMattMatt85: Instant history: a championship in 2024, just his third season, behind 2,099 points of pure fireworks. The sequel was less cinematic — a 2–12 title defense in 2025 that stands as the fastest fall from grace the league has ever witnessed. Champion to cellar in twelve months; even the trophy looked surprised.
summaries.espn13495523: One season, one finals run. Arrived in 2025, survived three separate games decided by tiebreaker — a full fifth of the league's all-time ties in a single debut — and marched a 7–7 roster to the championship game before RichoSuave ended the fairy tale. A debut that charmed deserves a banner someday. And maybe, eventually, an actual display name.
summaries.espn75676325: The best owner without a ring, full stop. A .604 career win rate, six playoff berths in seven seasons, and a six-game streak in 2024 — nobody active is more consistent. He's a perfect 6–0 against Rodney19140 and terrorizes the middle class. But 2–7–1 against kevinconklin05 and zero banners means the resume reads: great regular seasons, allergic to jewelry.
summaries.frolickingjester: The league's premier giant-slayer: 6–1 lifetime against two-time champ Dieselbaron, a five-game run in 2022, and a 2024 breakout (1,973 points). A dead-even 35–35 career suggests the best is coming. Against jmuggy20, however, he's 1–7 with one tie — the man owns him so thoroughly that even splitting a game evenly counts as frolickingjester's best result.
summaries.joe52690: Fifteen consecutive seasons of showing up — the league's iron man — crowned by a 2019 run to the final, a 2,014-point outburst in 2022, and a five-game streak that same year. Loyalty like that builds leagues. It also builds records: most career losses in history (122), a 1–12 campaign in 2014, and a 2–9 lifetime mark against frolickingjester. The heart of the league, if not its trophy case.
summaries.CheezeBallHustle: Nine seasons of grind with three playoff appearances, a genuine peak at 4th, and back-to-back-to-back-to-back wins in 2016. The exit was less dignified: a 2–11 farewell tour in 2020, and a career 1–9 record against adrenth01 that included a 136-point demolition. Some rivalries are competitive. That one was a subscription to pain.
summaries.Rodney19140: The audit vindicated him: hidden inside a decade of losing was a nine-game win streak in 2017 — quietly one of the longest runs in league history — plus a top-3 finish and a +115 knockout of eventual-champ adrenth01. His day came rarely otherwise: 43–88 overall, 0–6 against espn75676325, farmed by three different champions, and a 1–13 farewell in 2021. Beloved. Streaky. Farmed.
summaries.njohnson9352: Came out firing with 1,869 points as a rookie in 2011 — a debut most owners never top — and hung around for eight honest seasons (41–62–1), peaking at 5th. Unfortunately, the league's aristocracy treated him as a renewable resource: 1–10 against jstoll65, 7–1–1 the wrong way against b50rock, and the preferred victim of three different champions. A good man in a bad neighborhood.
summaries.Charlie Walls: One season, 2011, and more juice than the record shows: a four-game win streak and a 73-point statement win over future champion kevinconklin05. Still finished 5–8, ninth place, and walked away forever. Some men touch the flame once, get genuinely warm for a month, and decide it's hot anyway.
summaries.MarcusW054: Two founding seasons, 3–22–1, and the author of the most enduring record in league history: 913 points in 2010, the lowest-scoring season anyone has ever managed. Sixteen years later it still stands, untouched and possibly untouchable. He also played in the league's first-ever tied game — even his .500 moments came with an asterisk. Immortality finds us in strange ways.
summaries.brodywhite1012: A founding-era owner who gave it two seasons and 7 wins, with a best finish of 9th in 2009. His lone highlight reel is a win over MarcusW054 — which, historians note, was the fantasy equivalent of beating the practice squad. Gone by 2011, missed by few record books.
summaries.j5narlock: Two founding seasons, 11–15, and — credit where due — he closed 2010 on a three-game win streak. Retiring hot is a move most owners never master. The league will never know if it was the start of a dynasty or the universe's mercy rule.
summaries.ndirish1818: One season, 2011, finished 12th of 12 at 2–11. But within the wreckage: an 87-point ambush of juicebox269 that nobody saw coming, least of all juicebox269. Last place with one legendary scalp — there are worse ways to spend a single year.
summaries.rodneywoodcock: A two-season founding member who peaked at 7th in 2009 and put a 97-point hurting on future two-time champion adrenth01 along the way. The 2010 encore went 4–9, and that was that. Brief, occasionally violent, gone too soon.
